questions.questionText: What defines a robot's configuration space (C-space) in a 2D plane?
What constraint is characteristic of differential drive systems?

options.text: Zero turning radius at all times

questions.questionText: Which of the following limits linear acceleration and deceleration?
How can a differential drive robot turn in place?
What does the geometric shape (bounding circle or polygon) of a robot dictate?
In grid-based map representations, what is continuous floor space discretized into?

options.text: A uniform grid of individual cells

questions.questionText: Why is obstacle inflation necessary?

options.text: To eliminate all sensor noise completely
To convert the robot into a point mass while ensuring a safe physical clearance buffer
To increase the turning radius of the robot indefinitely
To speed up sensor reading cycles

questions.questionText: If a robot has a radius of 0.5 meters and a grid resolution of 0.1 meters per cell, by how many cells are obstacles inflated?
Which of the following is an inherent limitation of environmental maps?

options.text: Incompleteness, static obsolescence, and sensor noise

questions.questionText: What should a planned route through free grid cells always be treated as?

options.text: A tentative candidate subject to real-time verification
An obsolete piece of data that cannot be trusted

title: L16.3 — Sensors and Obstacle Detection Quiz

questions.questionText: What do ultrasonic and infrared (IR) sensors measure for short-range distance estimation?
What is a primary limitation of ultrasonic and infrared sensors?

options.text: Severe range limitations, narrow beams, and surface reflectivity dependencies
Inability to detect any obstacles at all
Complete immunity to ambient light and dust

questions.questionText: What do LiDAR units use to construct dense point clouds of surroundings?

options.text: Rotating or sweeping laser beams across a 360-degree plane

questions.questionText: Which filter is mentioned for accumulating sensor data over multiple sampling cycles with confidence weights?

options.text: Moving average filter, Kalman filter, or probabilistic occupancy grid

questions.questionText: How should a spurious echo from a dust particle be handled by the navigation system?

options.text: Cause erratic deviation in path planning
Be filtered out to prevent unnecessary stops or deviations
Automatically redefine the global goal coordinate

questions.questionText: What triggers an immediate stop command in reactive obstacle avoidance?

options.text: Frontal distance falling below a predefined safety stop threshold d_stop

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a common reactive obstacle avoidance strategy?
What is a primary strength of reactive obstacle avoidance strategies?

options.text: Complete immunity to local minima traps
Ultra-fast reaction time for handling sudden, unmapped dynamic obstacles
Comprehensive global awareness of the entire map

questions.questionText: What is a major limitation of purely reactive controllers?

options.text: They are too slow for real-world robotics
They frequently fall victim to local minima traps

questions.questionText: Why must optimal robotic architectures combine reactive behaviors with global path planning?

options.text: To eliminate all motors and actuators
To prevent getting stuck in local minima and ensure efficient long-term routing
To remove the need for sensor calibration
To increase wheel slip and friction

questions.questionText: How does Breadth-First Search (BFS) explore grid cells?

options.text: Uniformly outward layer by layer based strictly on step count
Using heuristic distance estimates to the goal
Prioritizing nodes with the lowest cumulative operational cost g(n)

questions.questionText: What is a major drawback of Breadth-First Search in robotics?

options.text: It fails to find the shortest step-count path
It explores in all directions equally and cannot naturally account for varying travel costs
It requires complex Euclidean distance formulas
It only works on continuous curves

questions.questionText: What does Dijkstra's algorithm evaluate nodes based on?

options.text: The exact operational cost g(n) incurred from the start node
Sensor noise and Gaussian error distributions

questions.questionText: What does the A* (A-star) search evaluation function f(n) consist of?
How is the heuristic estimate h(n) often calculated for grid-based robotics in A*?

options.text: Using motor torque and gear ratios
Using Euclidean distance or Manhattan distance formulas
Using wheel radius and track width

questions.questionText: What does a geometric path dictate in robotics engineering?

options.text: Where the robot should go spatially (without temporal parameters)
When the robot must arrive at specific timestamps
The exact motor torque curves and tire friction limits

questions.questionText: What does trajectory planning add to a geometric path?
Which physical limitations are integrated during trajectory planning?

options.text: Maximum linear velocity, peak acceleration limits, and braking deceleration distances
Matrix lookup values for static obstacles

questions.questionText: Why is optimal navigation route calculation fundamentally a time-optimization problem?

options.text: Because distance is always irrelevant in robotics
Because slowing down for sharp turns can result in longer travel times than smoother, longer curves
Because computers cannot calculate geometric paths without timestamps
Because robots cannot move in straight lines

questions.questionText: What velocity profiles are typically generated to ensure smooth trajectory execution?
What must an autonomous mobile robot analyze candidate paths for during minimum-time navigation?

options.text: Total route length and cumulative time cost during acceleration, cruising, and deceleration zones
Only the number of grid cells without regard to velocity
Ambient sunlight interference and lens distortion

questions.questionText: How is the turning velocity v_turn constrained around sharp turns by centripetal acceleration limits?
What does the emergency braking distance formula d_brake equal?
What is minimum-time navigation fundamentally described as?

options.text: An iterative constraint-satisfaction and optimization process balancing aggressiveness against safety
A method for eliminating all sensor noise

questions.questionText: Which physical factors are modeled in minimum-time navigation?

options.text: Robot mass, motor torque curves, friction coefficients, and safety envelopes

title: L16.8 — Dynamic Obstacles and Replanning Quiz

questions.questionText: What can block a previously calculated route long after initial mission planning is complete?

options.text: Moving obstacles such as pedestrians, other robots, or shifting objects
Constant wheel radii and track widths

questions.questionText: What does a continuous dynamic replanning loop require?

options.text: Halting the robot permanently upon any sensor reading
Repeatedly reading incoming sensor streams and evaluating path intersection
Ignoring all sensor inputs to maintain speed
Disabling the global path planner entirely

questions.questionText: What hazard must algorithms guard against during global path replanning?

options.text: Oscillation bugs (flip-flopping back and forth between detours due to symmetrical costs)
Excessive wheel slip caused by high motor torques

questions.questionText: What is paramount during dynamic obstacle encounters and replanning events?
What does a hierarchical control scheme combine in resilient navigation systems?

options.text: Global route planning with local, sensor-driven reactive updates
Ultrasonic sensors with infrared sensors only
Breadth-First Search with Dijkstra's algorithm without heuristics
Static maps with unchangeable obstacle footprints

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of building a 2D grid-world simulator in Python?

options.text: To replace physical machinery with expensive hardware immediately
To test and debug navigation logic before deploying onto physical hardware
To eliminate the need for pathfinding algorithms

questions.questionText: Which libraries are commonly used for Python grid-world simulators?

options.text: Pygame for animation or Matplotlib for static plotting
NumPy and Pandas for statistical database queries

questions.questionText: How is cell occupancy checked during simulation validation?

options.text: Via matrix lookups, ensuring if M[x][y] == 1, the coordinate is flagged as impassable
By measuring wheel slip and tire friction coefficients
By calculating exact time-of-flight ultrasound echoes

questions.questionText: What quantitative performance metrics do engineers track during simulator evaluation?

options.text: Total travel distance, simulated mission time, collision counts, and replanning frequency
Camera pixel density and frame rates
Motor gear ratios and electrical voltage drops

questions.questionText: What does simulated testing allow rapid iteration of?

options.text: Heuristic weights, speed profiles, and sensor noise models
Physical robot mass and chassis dimensions

questions.questionText: What phases does the cyclical execution structure of an autonomous robot separate?

options.text: Sensing, decision-making, and actuation into distinct phases
Acceleration, cruising, and braking into random sequences
Heuristic estimation and sensor noise into static matrices
Global path planning and obstacle inflation into single steps

questions.questionText: What does the pseudocode instruction sensor_data = read_sensors() accomplish?
What conditional check evaluates safety parameters inside the control loop?
What does the log_pose_and_time() function record at the conclusion of the loop?

options.text: Position coordinates, timestamps, and battery levels for post-mission evaluation
Ultrasonic sensor reflection intensity and camera focal lengths
Wheel radius and track width parameters
Centripetal force limits and tire slip coefficients

questions.questionText: What real-world engineering considerations must be addressed when deploying the control loop on hardware?

options.text: Precise sensor calibration, motor controller tuning, and fail-safe behavioral overrides
Infinite computational speed and zero latency
Eliminating all environmental obstacles from the physical world
Removing all safety margins and maximizing motor aggressiveness
